Messages.Author: Nancy L Feldman
Messages.Body:
1.  In a two-player game, how many transfers does the first 
player start with?  They seem to differentiate a "multi-player game" 
from a "two-player" game in this respect, so we couldn't tell if you
all (or rather, both) started with 4 transfers, or if the first 
player started with 1 and you worked your way toward 4.

2.  Several Jyhad cards indicate that you can "attack" any
of your prey's or predator's vampires.  Does attack in this instance
refer to initiating combat, or are we missing something?

3.  A very strange question.  Can someone describe the Clan symbol 
for the Malkavians, and the picture on Malkavian Time Auction.
Both have defeated my visual interpreter (the person who describes
uite well the picture on "Effective Management."d we like |q

Thanks in advance.  I'm sure we'll have more questions soon.

Nancy

Messages.Author: Doug DeJulio
Messages.Body:
In article <3340uc$lf5@pith.uoregon.edu>,
Nancy L Feldman <nfeldman@oregon.uoregon.edu> wrote:
>1.  In a two-player game, how many transfers does the first 
>player start with?  They seem to differentiate a "multi-player game" 
>from a "two-player" game in this respect, so we couldn't tell if you
>all (or rather, both) started with 4 transfers, or if the first 
>player started with 1 and you worked your way toward 4.

1) Normally you get 4 transfers per turn.
2) In a multiplayer game, the first 3 turns are different.

So, in a 2-player game, you get all 4 transfers on the first turns.

>2.  Several Jyhad cards indicate that you can "attack" any
>of your prey's or predator's vampires.  Does attack in this instance
>refer to initiating combat, or are we missing something?

Yeah, "attacking" someone means initiating combat.  If it's not
stealthy enough though, this action can be blocked by any other.  Then
the attacker would enter combat with the blocking Minion, instead of
the original chosen target.

The "Muddled Vampire Hunter" is like this, and it's a KILLER card.  I
traded mine away last night (because I only had two Malkavians).

>3.  A very strange question.  Can someone describe the Clan symbol 
>for the Malkavians, and the picture on Malkavian Time Auction.
>Both have defeated my visual interpreter (the person who describes
>uite well the picture on "Effective Management."d we like |q

The Malkavian Clan symbol is supposed to be a cracked hand mirror.

--

Messages.Author: Randall P.
Messages.Body:
Nancy L Feldman (nfeldman@oregon.uoregon.edu) wrote:
: 1.  In a two-player game, how many transfers does the first 
: player start with?  They seem to differentiate a "multi-player game" 
: from a "two-player" game in this respect, so we couldn't tell if you
: all (or rather, both) started with 4 transfers, or if the first 
: player started with 1 and you worked your way toward 4.

  Everyone gets four at all times. There is no differentiation between a 
2-player and multi-player game in this respect.

: 2.  Several Jyhad cards indicate that you can "attack" any
: of your prey's or predator's vampires.  Does attack in this instance
: refer to initiating combat, or are we missing something?

  Nope, you got it. Attacking is starting combat, unless it specifies 
otherwise.

: 3.  A very strange question.  Can someone describe the Clan symbol 
: for the Malkavians, and the picture on Malkavian Time Auction.
: Both have defeated my visual interpreter (the person who describes
: uite well the picture on "Effective Management."d we like |q

  The symbol represents a cracked mirror, indicative of the strange 
perceptions of these poor souls. The MTA card is more evocative than 
literal. The children of Malkav have the ability to affect time in 
strange ways, and communicate in ways fathomable only to their twisted 
minds. But try to get THEM to admit that! THEY refuse to even acknowledge 
that they are a clan!
  (This is paraphrasing some of the info from White Wolf's Clan Book: 
Malkavian)

: Thanks in advance.  I'm sure we'll have more questions soon.

: Nancy

Messages.Author: Brian Wilson
Messages.Body:
Before I could do anything to stop it, Randall P. wrote:

>   Everyone gets four at all times. There is no differentiation between a 
> 2-player and multi-player game in this respect.

Review the rules, section 12.4: Phase 3 - Influence

At the beginning of a multi-player game, the first few turns Methuselahs 
will have less than four transfers. On the first, second, and third turn,
a Methusela gets one, tow, or three transfers respectively; for example,
the Methuselah who goes third gets three transfers on that turn.

I read it like this:

	Player 1, turn 1: 1 transfers
	Player 2, turn 1: 2 transfers
	Player 3, turn 1: 3 transfers
	Player 4, turn 1: 4 transfers
	Player 1, turn 2: 4 transfers
	Player 2, turn 2: 4 transfers...

gets three, the fourth gets four.  All others get four.  Now, there is very
little point in limiting the transfers in a 2 player game since you are each
others prey/predator... but you're milage may vary...

Messages.Author: Cerebus The Aardvark
Messages.Body:
boardman@sun33.cs.wisc.edu (Daniel Boardman) writes:

>	Read the example. I think its flawed in that it contradicts the
>	rules... You and the book state you get 1 transfer for your first
>	turn, then 2 the next, etc, up till 4.. Heres the example:

>	Nora goes first in a 3 player game. She spends one transfer on
>	the card of a vampire, with, a six-point blood capacity. (1st turn)
>	On her next turn, she realizes she made a mistake for some reason,
>	in putting influence on that vampire, (2nd turn, uses 2 to remove
>	the 1 blood back to her pool) and as she, on her next turn, 
>	(turn 3, should have 3 transfers, correct?) recieves FOUR (!!)
>	transfers, <etc, etc>  

No, you misunderstood.  The first player to go gets one transfer, the
second player to go gets two, the third player to go gets three.  On Nora's
second turn, she is the fourth player to go, so she gets four transfers.
This is spelled out in the example text:

"On her next turn receives four transfers"

>	I dont think they proofread these things.. 

It's quite clear, you just misread it.  Re-read the whole example text.  On
Nora's SECOND turn she uses four transfers (two to remove a blood, two to
influence another vampire)

OK, I admit that they left the phrase "on her next turn" in twice, but
still.  It's her SECOND turn that she uses four transfers.  Otherwise the
example text would have her doing nothing on her second turn..

>	Read the example. I think its flawed in that it contradicts the

>	Nora goes first in a 3 player game. She spends one transfer on
>	the card of a vampire, with, a six-point blood capacity. (1st turn)
>	On her next turn, she realizes she made a mistake for some reason,
>	in putting influence on that vampire, (2nd turn, uses 2 to remove
>	the 1 blood back to her pool) and as she, on her next turn, 
>	(turn 3, should have 3 transfers, correct?) recieves FOUR (!!)
>	transfers, <etc, etc>  
>	I dont think they proofread these things.. 

No, the first Player get 1 transfer, the second player gets 2, the third
3 and every subsequent player gets 4.  So Nora going first get 1 transfer
on her first turn and (if in a multiplayer game) will get 4 on her next turn.

In a 2 player game between A & B I think is goes: A gets 1 on A's first turn
B then gets 2, then A get 3 and then they both get 4 from then on.

The idea is to keep the player who go first form overwhelming the others
due to have ing more minons earlier and so getting more actions.
